title: TEFL for Vietnam: TEFL, TESOL or CELTA? (2026)
description: What Vietnamese law requires (no 120-hour rule), what Saigon employers accept, online vs CELTA, 2026 CELTA dates and fees in HCMC, and accreditation red flags.
h1: TEFL, TESOL or CELTA for Vietnam: what the rules require, what employers accept and what it costs
intro: To teach at a licensed language centre in Vietnam you need a suitable teaching certificate on top of your degree, but no Vietnamese rule sets a minimum number of hours. Most Ho Chi Minh City chains accept an accredited 120-hour TEFL or TESOL, online courses included, while RMIT-level employers want a CELTA or equivalent. No certificate replaces the bachelor's degree the work permit asks for, and on its own none replaces the experience.
keyPoints: The law asks for a **suitable** teaching certificate at language centres (Circular 21/2018) and sets no hours: the 120-hour figure is what employers such as ILA and Apollo ask for, not a legal rule.
A TEFL, TESOL or CELTA does **not** replace the bachelor's degree, and on its own it does not replace the 2 years' experience in the work-permit test under Decree 219/2025/ND-CP.
Online 120-hour certificates are accepted by the big chains; a course with observed teaching practice with real learners makes your application stronger and prepares you for the demo lesson.

CELTA in Ho Chi Minh City runs at Apollo IH: {{vnd:42000000}} including Cambridge fees, or {{vnd:39500000}} if you pay at least 6 weeks before the start (fees as published in October 2026; for the 16 November course that deadline passed around 5 October). Full-time courses last four weeks; check the centre's course page for the next dates.
None of the 2025-2026 HCMC job ads we checked publishes a pay premium for a CELTA. What it does is open jobs that require it, such as RMIT's hourly educator roles.
Check any 'accredited' or 'Level 5' claim by awarding body and qualification number, not by the seller's badge.

sections.title: What the rules require, and what employers add

blocks.text: At a licensed language centre, a native-speaker foreign teacher needs a college (cao đẳng) degree or higher in any field plus a **'suitable' foreign-language teaching certificate** — that is the whole of [Circular 21/2018/TT-BGDĐT, Art. 18(5)](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-21-2018-tt-bgddt-quy-che-to-chuc-hoat-dong-cua-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-166595-d1.html). It names no degree subject and no minimum course length. The '120 hours' you see everywhere is an employer and market convention.

Which certificates count? In December 2020 the education ministry (MOET) wrote to Hanoi's labour department, which had been refusing them, recommending that TESOL, TEFL and CELTA be accepted, and named ALAP, Gatehouse Awards and Cambridge as examples of accrediting bodies ([Giáo dục Việt Nam's report](https://giaoduc.net.vn/bo-giao-duc-go-roi-quy-dinh-cap-phep-cho-giao-vien-tieng-anh-nuoc-ngoai-post214387.gd)). Official Letter 1105/HTQT from MOET's International Cooperation Department describes a suitable certificate as one accredited or recognised by a reputable international accreditation body, such as a TESOL, TEFL or CELTA, and says a course-completion certificate is not evidence equivalent to a degree ([LuatVietnam](https://luatvietnam.vn/linh-vuc-khac/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-thue-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-can-dieu-kien-gi-883-100926-article.html)).

blocks.text: The work permit is the real gate. [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025, replaced the foreign-worker rules of Decrees 152/2020 and 70/2023. Teachers are filed as 'experts': a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant work experience (Art. 3(3)(a)), down from 3. The usual proof is a letter from a past employer abroad; experience in Vietnam counts only through earlier Vietnamese work permits. For experts in education, Art. 19(3) also lists documents showing you meet the education-law qualification standard as an alternative proof, which is where your teaching certificate comes in.

How Ho Chi Minh City applies that alternative to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is **not published**, and nobody has confirmed whether a TEFL or CELTA practicum counts as experience. If you have less than 2 years, ask the employer which proof they will file and get the answer in writing before you travel — and never use an experience letter that is not true. Our [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) covers the procedure; the employer and the authority have the final word.

The city does check. In October 2025 HCMC's Department of Education and Training told its 1,961 licensed language and IT centres to tighten the management of foreign teachers ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-nang-cao-chat-luong-nhan-su-tai-cac-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-10388655.html)). In January 2026 it ordered schools running linked programmes to review teachers' qualifications; foreign teachers' files must include a work permit and translated, certified degrees, after inspections found teachers holding only course-attendance certificates and no pedagogy certificate ([Đại biểu Nhân dân](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html)).

blocks.title: A TEFL is not a way round the degree
blocks.text: The most expensive mistake is buying a 'TEFL plus guaranteed job' package in the hope that the certificate will stand in for a bachelor's degree. It will not: the expert route under Decree 219 needs a university degree, and none of the sources we checked supports a no-degree route for teaching. The full checklist is in [requirements to teach English in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/requirements-to-teach-english-in-vietnam).

sections.title: TEFL, TESOL, CELTA and Trinity CertTESOL compared

blocks.text: TEFL and TESOL are generic labels, not single qualifications: any provider can sell a course under either name, so the awarding body and the teaching practice matter more than the acronym. CELTA (Cambridge) and Trinity CertTESOL are specific, externally assessed qualifications with fixed standards wherever you take them.

blocks.text: CELTA is accredited by Ofqual at Level 5 of the UK Regulated Qualifications Framework, qualification number 501/1891/2 ([Cambridge](https://support.cambridgeenglish.org/hc/en-gb/articles/115004089423)). It does not require native-speaker status or teaching experience, but you need advanced English: IH Ho Chi Minh City asks for 'a proficient, advanced level of English' ([IH](https://ihteachenglish.com/?p=13232)).

Trinity CertTESOL is delivered only by Trinity-validated providers monitored by Trinity moderators ([Trinity College London](https://www.trinitycollege.com/qualifications/teaching-english/CertTESOL)). Trinity lists validated providers in Vietnam, but we could not confirm one in Ho Chi Minh City; use [Trinity's course finder](https://www.trinitycollege.com/site/?id=2093) before you plan around it.

sections.title: Is an online TEFL accepted in Vietnam?

blocks.text: Yes, at the big chains. [ILA](https://teachingenglish.ila.edu.vn/job-detail/?id=1) asks for a recognised qualification of 120 hours or more (TEFL Level 4 or higher, Ninja TESOL, AVSE TESOL, CELTA/Trinity or equivalent) and calls teaching practice 'highly preferred', not compulsory. [Apollo](https://www.theteflacademy.com/?p=61627) asks for an internationally recognised TEFL of at least 120 hours. A [VUS listing](https://teast.co/job/vus-the-leading-english-language-center-in-vietnam-is-looking-for-esl-teachers-VUSTheEngli1713981780000) accepts in-class and online courses, though [VUS's own FAQ](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979) prefers a course with an in-class component.

Where in-person training pays off is the hiring process itself. If an employer asks for a demo lesson, a course where a trainer watched you teach real learners gives you something to draw on — see [CVs, interviews and demo lessons](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-cv-and-demo-lesson-in-vietnam). A sensible floor, whichever format you choose: 120 hours or more printed on the certificate and at least 6 hours of observed, assessed teaching. That is practitioner advice, not a legal rule.

items: **Online 120-hour course, done before you fly:** fits around a job at home; enough for chain centres if accredited.

**In-person course in Saigon (about 4 weeks):** real classroom practice and a local network; ILA names Ninja TESOL and AVSE TESOL as acceptable, which is a useful sign that a local course is legitimate.
**CELTA or Trinity CertTESOL:** an intensive course of about 4–5 weeks full-time, or longer part-time; worth it if you are aiming at adults, universities or a long career in teaching.

sections.title: How to check a TEFL course before you pay

blocks.text: 'Accredited' means something only when an independent regulator or awarding body can be checked. These are the warning signs:

items: No named awarding body, or an 'accreditor' that turns out to be the provider's own brand.
No qualification number you can look up on a regulator's register.
No observed teaching practice with real learners at all.
A 'Level 5' label sold as if it made the course a CELTA: the level describes difficulty on the UK framework, not what the course contains.
'TEFL plus guaranteed job' bundles, especially ones aimed at people without a degree.

items.title: Ask for the awarding body and qualification number
items.text: A real UK-regulated qualification has both. CELTA's, for comparison, is 501/1891/2.

items.title: Look it up yourself
items.text: Check the number on the Ofqual Register (or the regulator the provider names), not on the seller's own badge page.

items.title: Confirm hours and practice on the certificate
items.text: The certificate itself should state the hours (120 or more). Ask how many hours of teaching with real learners are observed and assessed.

items.title: Ask your target employers before you buy
items.text: Email two or three centres you would apply to and ask whether they accept that exact course. Employers decide this, not Vietnamese law. Recruiters who want a fee for a job are a separate red flag — see [teaching job scams](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Taking a CELTA in Ho Chi Minh City: dates and fees

blocks.text: The CELTA centre we could confirm in Ho Chi Minh City is **Apollo IH Ho Chi Minh City** (International House, part of Apollo English). Its published full-time, face-to-face intakes run 9:00–17:30 on weekdays ([IH course page](https://www.ihteachenglish.com/course/3726)).

blocks.text: IH has also run a part-time hybrid course (7 September to 6 November 2026), so ask about the next one if you are already working. IH's pages disagree on where training happens — one says the District 3 centre, another Binh Thanh — so confirm the address. Since July 2025 official addresses use new ward names; former District 3 is now Ban Co, Xuan Hoa and Nhieu Loc wards.

IH says it provides no formal accommodation support, so book your own. On the [eno.vn HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) (snapshot 10 October 2026), the median asking rent for a room is {{vnd:4650000}} a month in District 3 and {{vnd:4500000}} a month in Binh Thanh; you can search [rooms and apartments](/c/rentals) near the centre once you know the address.

For comparison, International House London's 2026 price list puts its CELTA at £1,747 plus a £186 Cambridge assessment fee ([IH London](https://www.ihlondon.com/?p=74058)). We could not confirm a Cambridge Delta course in Vietnam for 2026; the Delta is the next step after a CELTA, covered in [career paths for English teachers](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-career-path-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Does a CELTA raise your pay in Ho Chi Minh City?

blocks.text: Not directly, as far as published ads show. **None of the 2025-2026 HCMC job ads we checked publishes a pay premium for a CELTA.** In July–October 2026 ads, centres offered foreign teachers {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, with most new-teacher offers at {{vnd:430000-560000}} an hour ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs listings](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh)), and most of those centres accept any accredited 120-hour TEFL. Claims that a CELTA adds a fixed amount a month come from course sellers and are not backed by published ads.

What a CELTA does is open the doors that a basic TEFL does not. RMIT Vietnam's 2026 hourly educator role requires a bachelor's degree, a CELTA or equivalent and at least 3 years' post-CELTA experience; non-native speakers need IELTS Academic 8.0 with no band below 7.5 ([RMIT position description](https://www.rmit.edu.au/content/dam/rmit/au/en/careers/position-descriptions/vietnam/JD-Educator%20July%202026.pdf)). RMIT's last published rate, in an ad that closed in December 2023, was US$30.55 an hour gross for expat candidates. Wall Street English in Ho Chi Minh City says a CELTA or Trinity certificate, or an MA in TESOL, is 'strongly preferred', though it may consider other equivalent TEFL qualifications ([the ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/ho-chi-minh-city-part-time-native-english-teachers-2)).

For the bigger jumps in pay, the certificate is not the lever: international schools pay for a home-country teaching licence and experience, not a TEFL (see [international school jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam)). The full picture of rates, hours and take-home pay is in [English teacher salary in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam).

blocks.text: Young learners: Cambridge discontinued the CELTA Young Learner extension in December 2016 and points to TKT: Young Learners instead ([Cambridge](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/teaching-english/teaching-courses-and-modules-discontinued)). An ad still asking for 'CELTA YL' is out of date. VUS says most of its students are 6 to 16, so for most centre jobs a children's focus matters more than the brand of certificate — see [teaching young learners](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-young-learners-in-vietnam).

Non-native speakers: the law does not bar you, but a non-native teacher with an unrelated degree needs both C1-level proof and a teaching certificate. The rule names no test; IELTS 7.0 or above is the common working benchmark, and recruiters often quote 6.5–7.0+. A CELTA is open to you if your English is at an advanced level. Employer practice is stricter than the law — see [hiring bias in teaching jobs](/teach-in-vietnam/discrimination-and-hiring-bias-in-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Getting the certificate ready for your work permit file

blocks.text: Ask your employer early whether your teaching certificate goes into the work-permit file or the centre's own teacher file. If it does, treat it like your degree. Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from 11 September 2026 ([HCCH status table](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41); [Decree 293/2026/ND-CP](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/decree-no-293-2026-nd-cp-dated-july-23-2026-of-the-government-providing-guidance-on-the-implementation-of-the-hague-convention-dated-october-05-196-441290-doc1.html)): documents from member countries need an apostille, while documents from Germany, Austria and Czechia, which objected, and from non-member countries still need consular legalisation ([Rödl & Partner](https://www.roedl.com/en/insights/update-vietnam-thehague-apostille-convention/)). Thailand's membership takes effect only on 28 February 2027, so a certificate issued by a course provider in Thailand still needs consular legalisation until then. A certified Vietnamese translation follows in Vietnam.

items: Get the apostille or legalisation in the country that issued the certificate, before you fly; ask the employer which format the HCMC office is accepting right now. The details by country are in [getting your degree and documents authenticated](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam).
Bring the originals of your degree, transcript and certificates plus copies. An employer may not keep your original degree or certificates.
Some employers pay for this: VUS says it reimburses all teachers' document-authentication fees. Ask before you spend.

blocks.text: Once you are certified, you can list the qualification on a free eno.vn teacher profile (start at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn)), where schools and centres can find you, and browse employers in the [Saigon school directory](/schools).

faqs.q: Is a 100-hour TEFL enough to teach in Vietnam?
faqs.a: The law sets no minimum, but the main chains ask for 120 hours or more: ILA and Apollo both state it. A few employers accept less, so a 100-hour certificate narrows your options rather than ruling you out. If you are choosing now, take 120 hours or more.

faqs.q: Can I teach in Vietnam with a TEFL but no bachelor's degree?
faqs.a: Not legally on a work permit. The expert route under Decree 219/2025 needs a university degree plus experience; a TEFL, TESOL or CELTA does not substitute for the degree and, on its own, does not substitute for the experience. Be wary of packages that promise otherwise.

faqs.q: Does it matter whether my certificate says TEFL or TESOL?
faqs.a: No. MOET's guidance names TESOL, TEFL and CELTA, and ILA and VUS accept either label. What employers check is the hours, the awarding body and whether teaching practice was included.

faqs.q: When is the next CELTA in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: In October 2026 Apollo IH Ho Chi Minh City listed full-time courses from 16 November to 11 December 2026 and from 4 to 29 January 2027, 9:00 to 17:30. The November course's early-payment price closed around 5 October. Dates and the early-payment deadline (at least 6 weeks before the start) change, so check the centre's course page before you plan around one.

faqs.q: Does a TEFL or CELTA practicum count as teaching experience for the work permit?
faqs.a: This has not been confirmed. Experience is normally proved with a letter from a past employer abroad or an earlier Vietnamese work permit, so ask your employer what they will file before you rely on course hours.
